law: Employees' time is not CSR spend
MCA has said monetising employees' pro bono services does not count towards the 2% CSR obligation.
CSR staff salaries fall in the 5% overhead cap
Salaries of regular CSR staff and of employees who render services for CSR are administrative overheads, capped at 5% of CSR spend.
Activities that benefit only employees and their families are not CSR — so team meals, T-shirts or travel for volunteers can't be booked as CSR.
Costs of the community project itself (materials, kits, NGO costs) can be CSR if the activity fits Schedule VII and runs through an eligible channel.
MCA encourages companies to involve employees in CSR, so volunteering strengthens CSR projects without adding to the spend.

steps: Ask partner NGOs what help they actually need; avoid 'volunteer tourism' that costs NGOs more than it gives.
Paid volunteer days, who is eligible (contract staff, families, retirees), approvals and leave tracking.
Mix easy entry points (events, virtual) with deeper skills-based and long-term roles.
Child-protection and POSH rules, background checks for work with children, insurance, travel and data-privacy protocols.
Site or team SPOCs, ERG leads and leadership role models to drive participation.
One platform or calendar for sign-up, logging hours and sharing stories.
Certificates, volunteer grants, awards and leadership shout-outs.
